title: Caching Common Development Dependencies knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Caching Common Development Dependencies?
options: Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.

questions.answer_key: Cache keys should reflect package manager, OS/runtime, and dependency lockfiles so changed dependencies invalidate stale cached inputs.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of caching common development dependencies: Cache keys should reflect package manager, OS/runtime, and dependency lockfiles so changed dependencies invalidate stale cached inputs. questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to caching common development dependencies?
options: Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: Cache keys should reflect package manager, OS/runtime, and dependency lockfiles so changed dependencies invalidate stale cached inputs.
